findings.title: The S=3 candidate count is wrong, so the expected gain is overstated
findings.description:
Line 58 says "With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000" and "With both: candidates loaded ~555". With `cell_size = r/3`, a 7×7 scan covers 49 cells × ~555 agents, which is about **27,000** candidates. That is (2S+1)²/S² = 5.4 r² of area, against 9 r² at S=1, so only about 1.65× fewer. The source analysis in `148-notes.rediagnosis.md` (lines 108–111) gives this correct figure. The slice doc misquotes it.

This matters for planning. Almost all of the expected gain comes from early exit. In dense regions subdivision adds little on top, because the cap is usually reached inside the first cell scanned. Fix line 58 so the A2/A3 expectations and the gate setting `S=3` are based on the right numbers. Also say what S=3 is expected to add once early exit is in place. If the answer is "little," consider defaulting gate runs to S=1 and keeping subdivision as a measured option.

findings.title: Step 3 cannot separate the two interventions
findings.description:
Two pairs of commands in Step 3 are identical: "Baseline (counter-gating)" and "Early exit only" both use `--subdivision-factor 1`, and "Subdivision only" and "Both" both use `--subdivision-factor 3`. The design adds the `break` unconditionally (lines 36–46) and defines no early-exit switch. So on this slice's code, the "Baseline … should reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS" run will not reproduce slice 145.

The lighter fix is to drop the four-way comparison. Measure the baseline once on the slice 145 commit, or use the recorded 38 TPS from `145-notes.fused-tick-measurements.md`. Then run S=1 and S=3 with early exit. Adding an early-exit switch only to support a comparison run is configuration that nothing else would use.

findings.title: `cell_size` and `S` can disagree, and a mismatch silently drops neighbors
findings.description:
The diagram lists `cell_size (= query_radius / S)` and `subdivision_factor S` as two separate `BenchConfig` fields. Line 80 says the harness "reads [cell_size] from config." If both can be set independently, a config like `cell_size=16.7, S=1` scans only ±1 cell of 16.7 units. Neighbors between about 16.7 and 50 units away are never seen, and nothing reports an error. That breaks the claim on line 56 that the "correct neighborhood is preserved."

The validation block on lines 69–76 checks `S` alone. Either compute `cell_size = query_radius / S` in one place and remove it as a separate input (preferred, single source of truth), or add a config-time check that `cell_size * S >= query_radius` and raise on failure. Do not rely on the defaults being consistent.

findings.title: No test checks that the (2S+1)² scan covers the same neighborhood
findings.description: The only correctness gates for subdivision are A1 (the existing slice 145 parity tests, which run at S=1) and A4 (statistical parity within 20%). A bug in the generalized loop could pass a 20% tolerance on mean speed and mean nearest-neighbor distance. Examples are an off-by-one like `range(-S, S)`, or an error converting cell coordinates near boundaries at the smaller cell size. The design already keeps the uncapped path (`max_neighbors = 0`, line 46), which makes a deterministic test cheap: in uncapped mode, S=1 and S=3 must find the same set of neighbors within radius, so forces should match to floating-point accumulation tolerance. Add this as a criterion so line 56's claim is actually tested.

findings.title: The design doesn't say how `S` reaches the production engine (slice 146)
findings.description:
Line 116 justifies A3 (≥100 TPS) as headroom "before slice 146 wires the GPU tick into the production engine." Line 111 calls `S` a bench configuration input and says 146 is unblocked. The default is S=1. If `subdivision_factor` exists only in `BenchConfig` and the `--subdivision-factor` CLI flag, the live server gets S=1. The headroom measured at S=3 then does not apply to the path that must meet the Tier 2 NFR (60 TPS at N=50k on the live world server).

State where `subdivision_factor` lives: in a backend or engine config that both the bench harness and the slice 146 production path read, or explicitly bench-only with 146 owning the plumbing. Also state which S value the A3 headroom claim applies to in production.

findings.title: The NFR is restated with its target
findings.description: The design cites the 60 TPS at N=50k Tier 2 target and sets A3 at ≥100 TPS. Both match the exit criteria in the slice plan entry. A2 (≥5× `force_total`) and A4 (20% statistical parity) also match the plan.

findings.title: Dependencies and boundaries are correct
findings.description: The design depends only on 145 and does not change `TickResult`, the world-server boundary, the numpy/numba backends or the agent state layout. That matches the plan's "the tick return type contract is the only shared interface" decision. Slice 148's tiled kernel is removed before merge (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md` §Disposition), so the `break` cannot conflict with cooperative shared-memory loads.

findings.title: Failure handling is fail-fast and proportionate
findings.description: The slice adds no new I/O paths or message types. The one new input, `S`, is checked at config load with an explicit `ValueError` rather than clamped, which follows the project's rule against silent fallbacks. No guard is needed inside the kernel.

findings.title: Name the S upper bound as a constant
findings.description: The literal `8` appears in both the comparison and the error message. Define it once as a named constant, following the project rule on comparison values. Also note that `isinstance(True, int)` is true in Python, so `S=True` would pass validation as 1.

findings.title: Scan order biases first-k-found neighbors toward one corner
findings.description: Scanning starts at `(drow, dcol) = (-S, -S)`. In dense regions the cap fills from cells on the −x/−y side, so the accepted neighbor set is lopsided. Slice 145 already has this bias at S=1, so it isn't new here. The A4 metrics (mean speed, mean nearest-neighbor distance) would not detect a directional drift. Worth one sentence of acknowledgement. Fixing it belongs with the distance-ranked swap (A7), not this slice.

findings.title: The `break` was only tested on Metal; cite that test
findings.description: Line 29 says Quadrants supports `break` in inner loops but not the outermost parallel loop, without citing evidence. `145-notes.phase-2-risk-poc.md` §2.1 confirmed that an inner-loop `break` compiles and runs correctly, but only on Metal. Cite that note and treat the CUDA build as the first check during implementation, since CUDA is the gate target.

findings.title: The plan's 7-neighbor benchmark point isn't mentioned
findings.description: The slice plan entry calls "the 7-neighbor operating point … a benchmark target." The design's gate config uses only `max_neighbors=32`. One extra run at `max_neighbors=7`, with no gate attached, would cover it. Otherwise, say explicitly that it is deferred.
